newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand broke out of a tight trading range to probe the 4.44 level in late Wednesday trade as the dollar posted fresh highs against the Deutschmark in late European trade.

At 1400 GMT, the rand was pegged at 4.4365/4395 against the dollar from 4.4320/4350 overnight. It touched a day's weakest level of 4.4380 bid shortly before the local close after trading in a 4.4270 to 4.4340 range for much of the day.
In late London afternoon trade, the dollar rose to a two-year high against the mark when it touched 1.7211 marks. Earlier the dollar rose to a 56-month high of 126.92 against the Japanese yen.
The rand's move weaker late in the day came after the market had been caught slightly short dollars, a dealer said, after a day of steady local importer demand for the U.S. unit.
Supply on the day came from varying sources, dealers said, citing both offshore and exporter dollar selling, with some suggesting the Reserve Bank had also been on the offer side during the day.

Dealers said the currency's weakness on the day, which brought its losses against the dollar to almost three cents in as many days, was in line with the dollar's resurgence against the major currencies.
They said a break above the 4.44 level appeared likely, after which dealers said the rand would target the 4.45 level before the end of the week.
"With the dollar being so strong, the 4.45 level is possible," a senior trader said.

The dollar's strength drove the rand to fresh highs against the crosses on the day. The local unit touched a fresh 14-month high of 28.6618 yen and 0.3884 marks earlier, while sterling held steady at around the 7.20 mark.
Bonds put in another dull performance as volumes remained low, interest subdued and direction nowhere in sight.
The key R150 was last quoted at a 15.18 percent from 15.135 percent overnight after trading in a 15.13 to 15.18 range during the day.
Dealers said that trade on the day had generally been thin, with local jobber sales of stock being absorbed by offshore buying.
"Its been a scrappy market with not much volumes," a trader said.
Direction could come in the form of February producer inflation data at 0900 GMT on Thursday, although trader did not hold out much hope that the data would move the market.
A Reuters consensus poll of economicsts forecast PPI would rise 0.7 percent in February after rising 0.8 percent in January.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.65 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate held its recent 15.95 to 16.15 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage dropped more than a billion rand on Tuesday, falling to 8.899 billion rand from 9.972 billion rand on Monday.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 156.90 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 99.99 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.25 billion rand, up from 2.73 billion rand on Monday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
